verified_opportunities.title: InvoicePulse v3 — Zero-Subscription Overdue Invoice Command Center
verified_opportunities.buyer_persona: Solo freelance developers, designers, and boutique consultants
verified_opportunities.recurring_pain: Losing hours weekly writing awkward unpaid-invoice follow-up emails and watching AP quietly overlook invoices, while resenting $25-$59/mo CRM suites and 4%-6.9% SaaS fee markups.
verified_opportunities.current_workaround: Manual Gmail reminders + spreadsheets or overpaying for bloated CRM subscriptions
verified_opportunities.urgency_signal: Direct cashflow delay and recurring monthly subscription fatigue

evidence.verbatim_quote: I kept losing hours every week writing 'just checking in' emails for unpaid invoices — and I knew every other freelancer was doing the same.

The invoicing SaaS I was using to bill my clients raised its credit card processing fee to 6.9% for free accounts (4% on top of Stripe's 2.9% + 30c fee), so I decided to build my own to fit my minimal needs.
I thought I had a good relationship with one client and that invoices were being paid on time, but then I found that around £10k had been overlooked by AP over the course of a few years.
The idea came from repeatedly watching freelancers (and honestly, myself) lose time to admin just to get paid.

verified_opportunities.title: ScopeShield — Zero-Subscription Freelance Change-Order & Scope-Creep Generator
verified_opportunities.buyer_persona: Fixed-price freelance developers, designers, and boutique agencies
verified_opportunities.recurring_pain: Losing 20%-40% of project margin to casual client 'quick tweak' DMs because drafting formal change orders feels confrontational and proposal suites cost $39-$65/user/mo.
verified_opportunities.current_workaround: Absorbing unpaid extra hours or manually rewriting Word/Google Doc addendums
verified_opportunities.urgency_signal: Immediate unbilled margin loss and launch-blocker delays

evidence.verbatim_quote: One pro habit you need is dealing with change orders and part of that has to do with whether you have an easier or more difficult client to please. For example, a difficult client will ask for 'tweak' but if you're a pro, you don't bite.
On the flip side I've seen many projects go way over budget when a client is actively involved and introduces scope creep that turns into launch blockers.
This is so true, scope creep is real when the client actively gets involved And when that happens it's better to move the contract to hourly rather having it fixed price

verified_opportunities.buyer_persona: Indie hackers, solo SaaS founders, and small web agencies shipping landing pages
verified_opportunities.recurring_pain: Shipping day-one launch bugs (broken links, missing OG/SEO tags, missing security headers) because enterprise SEO audit suites cost $49-$249/month.
verified_opportunities.current_workaround: Manually viewing page source or paying $99-$139/mo for bloated SEO suites
verified_opportunities.urgency_signal: Day-one launch traffic wasted on broken social cards, SEO tags, or security warnings

evidence.verbatim_quote: I built Shipcheck after seeing too many launches where small technical issues caused real problems on day one — broken links, slow pages, misconfigured SSL, missing security headers, DNS/email setup mistakes, etc.

I've been building CheckSitePulse, a website auditing tool that crawls sites and reports issues like broken links, spelling mistakes, accessibility problems, SEO issues, missing security headers, and content policy violations.
The main difference is it bundles a bunch of launch checks in one place like SEO metadata, sitemap/robots, security headers

verified_opportunities.title: SubTrim — Zero-Plaid Local CSV Subscription & SaaS Leak Auditor
verified_opportunities.buyer_persona: Privacy-conscious solo founders, developers, and freelancers
verified_opportunities.recurring_pain: Refusing to hand over bank usernames/passwords/MFA to Plaid-connected budgeting apps ($14.99/mo YNAB/Monarch) while silently bleeding cash to forgotten recurring SaaS renewals and price hikes.
verified_opportunities.current_workaround: Manually eyeballing monthly PDF/CSV bank statements or skipping audits entirely
verified_opportunities.urgency_signal: Immediate cash savings plus strong security aversion to sharing bank credentials

evidence.verbatim_quote: Plaid needing you to enter your username, password, and MFA for your bank is like genuine lunacy.
Plaid requires your bank username and password, so they have full read-write access to your account. They can do anything you can do when logged in to the bank's website
unexpected charges and difficult-to-cancel billing is the game. The best customer is always the one that pays but never uses the service

evidence.verbatim_quote: Writing changelogs is tedious and usually skipped. I built changelogai.to: connect your GitHub account, select a repo, and AI generates customer-friendly changelogs directly from your commit history.

I'm building a changelog system at the moment. It's basically the github_changelog_generator gem, but without overwriting old changelog entries.
